author: Philip Newman Lawton
book_description:
Philip Newman Lawton's work is like hearing from a friend.--Susan Shafarzek, 
Streetlight Magazine
Few writers are as gifted in beautifully crafting short works with such profoundly rich content.--Jon D. Wisman, American UniversityIf you're wondering what distinguishes us from the rest of the sentient world, Philip Newman Lawton has taken notes.--Ron Berube, author of 
The Tearing Sound
Philip Newman Lawton holds a PhD degree (docteur) in philosophy from the French-speaking section of the Catholic University of Louvain and an MBA degree from Northeastern University. Formerly an investment professional at major insurance companies and international banks, he now reads and writes in rural Virginia. The first part of Last Call is creative a selection of memoir pieces about the author's youth, education, ad career, along with his lifelong struggle for mental health. The second part contains highly readable essays on modern thinkers and writers, including Descartes, Rousseau, Bergson, John Henry Newman, Edith Stein, Samuel Beckett, Marguerite Yourcenar, and the twentieth-century Czech philosopher Jan Patocka. Most of these narratives and commentaries originally appeared in little magazines and literary journals.Show more
